(Note)

The reason they refrained from conjugating verbs such as ويله (waylahu), ويحه (waylahu/wayḥahu), ويسه (waysahu) and ويبه (waybahu) is that this is a *lafif maqrun* (a root with two weak letters, a "doubly weak" root). If they had formed a verb from it, the waw would have come after the present-tense prefix letter, and that would require its elision, as in يعد (ya'idu), يزن (yazinu) and يثق (yathiqu). The 'ayn would also be a weak letter, and the third radical would be weak as well. That would require moving its vowel to the preceding consonant and making it quiescent, as in يبيع (yabi'u) and يحيد (yahidu). Thus a series of weakening rules would apply to one word, and they did not permit this, so they rejected the verb altogether.

(Note)

Every verb that requires an object and seeks it, but does not reach it by itself, is connected to it by an instrument, which is the preposition (ḥarf al-jarr).

Then they may omit the preposition when the verb includes the meaning of a verb that is transitive by itself, as has been mentioned before. But here there is a subtle point that should be noticed: a verb may be transitive by itself to one object and to another by means of a preposition, and then the object that is reached directly is omitted because the listener knows it, while the one reached by the preposition remains, as they say: نصحت لزيد (I advised Zayd), كلت له (I measured for him), ووزنت له (I weighed for him), وشكرت له (I thanked him).

In all of this the object is omitted, and the verb reaches the other by means of the preposition.

Their saying that there are four verbs that are transitive by themselves at times and by a preposition at other times, and that they mention these, is not heard, because it is a bare statement lacking verification. Rather, the object is in reality omitted.

Your saying "نصحت له" is derived from نصح الخياط الثوب (the tailor mended the garment) when he repaired it and joined its parts together. Then it was used figuratively for opinion, and they said: نصحت له أي نصحت له رأيه, meaning I purified and corrected his opinion for him.

The phrase التوبة النصوح (sincere repentance) is derived from this, for sin tears the religion, so sincere repentance is like the tailor's mending of the garment when he repairs it and joins its parts. They say نصحت زيدا, dropping the preposition, because advice is guidance, as if you had said: أرشدته (I guided him).

Likewise شكرت is only an intensification and exaltation of the verb, from شكر بطنه (his belly became full).

So the original is شكرت لزيد إحسانه وفعله (I thanked Zayd for his kindness and his deed), then you omit the object and say شكرت لزيد, then you omit the preposition, because شكرت includes the meaning of حمدت (I praised) or مدحت (I commended).

As for كلت لزيد and وزنت له, their object is other than Zayd, because what they seek is what is measured or weighed.

So the original is the entry of the lam, and then it may be omitted for added benefit, because measuring and weighing food includes the meaning of trading and bartering, except when the lam is present.

If you say كلت لزيد, you have informed of measuring food only, and if you say كلت زيدا, you have informed of dealing and trading with him along with measuring, as if you had said: بايعته بالكيل والوزن (I traded with him by measure and weight). For taking a thing, such as buying, measuring and purchasing and the like, its verb includes drawing to oneself and carrying to one's own load what the giver and seller do not include.

**Chapter: Sins Remove Modesty**

Among the punishments of sins is the loss of *haya'* (modesty, a sense of shame before God), which is the substance of the heart's life. It is the root of every good, and its loss is the loss of all good.

In the *Sahih* it is related from him (ﷺ) that he said: "Modesty is entirely good."

He (ﷺ) also said: "Among what people have obtained from the words of the earlier prophethood is: 'If you have no shame, then do as you wish.'" There are two interpretations of this:

The first is that it is a threat and a warning. The meaning is: whoever has no shame will do whatever ugly deeds he wishes, since what restrains a person from them is modesty. When there is no modesty to restrain him from ugliness, he will commit it. This is the interpretation of Abu 'Ubayda.

The second is that if you do not feel shame before God about an act, then do it. What should be avoided is only that which one feels shame about before God. This is the interpretation of Imam Ahmad in the narration of Ibn Hani'.

On the first interpretation, it is a threat, like His saying: ﴿Do whatever you wish﴾ [Fussilat: 40].

On the second, it is a permission and a license.

If it is asked: Is there any way to read it as carrying both meanings?

I say: No, nor according to the view of those who take a homonym (*al-mushtarak*, a word with several meanings) to carry all its meanings at once, because there is a contradiction between permission and threat. But recognizing one of the two meanings necessitates recognizing the other.

The point is that sins weaken a servant's modesty, until perhaps it strips away from him altogether. He may not be affected even by people's knowledge of his bad condition or their witnessing of it. Indeed, many of them report their own state and the ugliness of what they do, and what moves them to this is their stripping away of modesty. When a servant reaches this state, there remains no hope for his righteousness.

A poet said:

*"And when Iblis sees the radiance of his face, he feels shame and says: 'I would ransom one who does not prosper.'"*

Modesty (*haya'*) is derived from life (*hayah*). Rain is called *haya'* (with a short vowel, *hay*), because by it the earth, the plants and the animals have life. Likewise, the life of this world and the Hereafter has been named by modesty. Whoever has no modesty is dead in this world and wretched in the Hereafter. Between sins and the scarcity of modesty and the absence of jealousy (*ghayrah*) there is a mutual necessity from both sides; each calls for the other and seeks it urgently. Whoever feels shame before God when he disobeys Him, God will feel shame to punish him on the day he meets Him. And whoever does not feel shame about his disobedience, God will not feel shame about punishing him.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Allah, glorified is He, inscribed the book of the wicked (fujjar) in the lowest part of the earth, so they are acting in accordance with what was inscribed for them in that book.

And He inscribed the book of the righteous (abrar) and placed it in 'Illiyyun (the highest level of Paradise), so they are brought [to act] until they do what has been inscribed for them in that book.

He, glory be to Him, informed that their earning had covered their hearts and prevented them from believing in His signs, so they said: ﴿Tales of the ancients﴾.

Some of the early generation (al-salaf, the pious predecessors) said regarding His words, ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾, that it is sin after sin.

Al-Hasan said: It is sin upon sin, until it blinds the heart.

Others said: When their sins and disobediences multiplied, they encompassed their hearts.

The root of this is that the heart rusts from disobedience. When it increases, the rust overcomes it until it becomes ran (rust-covering). Then it prevails further until it becomes ṭab' (sealing), qufl (a lock) and khatm (a seal), so the heart is in a veil (ghishāwah) and a covering (ghilāf). If this happens to it after guidance and insight, its upper part becomes its lower part, and then its enemy takes charge of it and drives it wherever he wishes.

He said in (al-Madārij):

"Al-raynu" and "al-rānn" are the thick veil that prevents the heart from seeing the truth and submitting to it.

He said in (Shifā' al-'Alīl):

As for al-rān, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾.

Abū 'Ubaydah said: It overcame it. Wine "yurayyinu" (clouds) the intellect of the drunkard, and death "yurayyinu" over the dead, so it takes him away. From this is the hadith of Usay'a of Juhaynah.

And the saying of 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): "Fa-aṣbaḥa qadriynan bihi," meaning it overcame him and the rayn encompassed him.

Abū Mu'ādh al-Naḥwī said: al-rayn is that the heart becomes black from sins.

And al-ṭab': that it be sealed upon the heart. It is stronger than al-rayn.

And al-aqfāl (locks) are stronger than al-ṭab': that it be locked upon the heart.

Al-Farrā' said: Their sins and disobediences multiplied, so they encompassed their hearts; that is the rayn upon them.

Abū Ishāq said: Rāna means covered. It is said: sin rānā upon his heart, yarīnu, raynan, meaning it overcame it.

He said: Al-rayn is like a covering that veils the heart, and similarly al-ghayn.

I say: Abū Ishāq erred. Al-ghayn is the subtlest and most delicate thing.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Indeed, there comes over my heart (ghayn), and I seek forgiveness from Allah a hundred times a day."

As for al-rayn and al-rān, it is among the thickest and densest veils over the heart.

Mujāhid said: It is sin upon sin, until sins surround the heart and cover it, and the heart dies.

Muqātil said: Their evil deeds overwhelmed the hearts.

In Sunan al-Nasā'ī and al-Tirmidhī, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said:

"When the servant commits a sin, a black spot is marked on his heart. If he gives it up, seeks forgiveness and repents, his heart is polished. If he increases (in sin), it increases until it covers his heart. That is the rān of which Allah spoke: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾."

Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a ṣaḥīḥ (sound) hadith.

'Abdullāh ibn Mas'ūd said: "Every time he sins, a black spot is marked on his heart, until the whole heart becomes black."

So He, glory be to Him, informed that their sins which they earned necessitated rayn upon their hearts; thus the cause of the rayn came from them.

And it is Allah's creation in them. He is the Creator of the cause and its effect, but the cause is by the servant's choice, and the effect is beyond his power and choice.

(Benefit)

The heart rusts through two things: heedlessness (ghafla) and sin; and its polishing is through two things: seeking forgiveness and remembrance (dhikr).

Whoever's heedlessness dominates his times, the rust accumulates upon his heart, and its rust is in proportion to his heedlessness. When the heart rusts, the images of knowledge are not impressed upon it as they are, so it sees falsehood in the form of truth and truth in the form of falsehood, because when rust accumulates upon it, it darkens, and the forms of realities do not appear in it as they really are.

When rust accumulates upon it, becomes black, and rān covers it, its perception and understanding are corrupted, so it accepts no truth and rejects no falsehood.

This is the greatest punishment of the heart.

The root of that is heedlessness and following desire, for they obliterate the light of the heart and blind its sight. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who followed his desire, and whose affair was excess﴾.

(Section)

Imam Aḥmad said: al-Walīd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Awzā'ī say: I heard Bilāl ibn Sa'd say: "Do not look at the smallness of the sin, but look at whom you have disobeyed."

Al-Fuḍayl ibn 'Iyāḍ said: In proportion as the sin seems small to you, it becomes great with Allah, and in proportion as it seems great to you, it becomes small with Allah.

It was said: Allah revealed to Moses: "O Moses, the first of My creatures to die is Iblīs, for he was the first to disobey Me. I only count those who disobeyed Me among the dead."

In the Musnad and the Jāmi' of al-Tirmidhī, from the hadith of Abū Ṣāliḥ, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when the believer commits a sin, a black spot is marked on his heart. When he repents, gives it up and seeks forgiveness, his heart is polished. If he increases (in sin), it increases until it covers his heart. That is the rān of which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spoke: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 14]."

Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a ṣaḥīḥ hadith.

Ḥudhayfah said: When the servant commits a sin, a black spot is marked on his heart until his heart becomes like a spotted (rayda') sheep.

Imam Aḥmad said: Ya'qūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn Shihāb, Ubayd Allāh ibn 'Abd Allāh ibn 'Utbah narrated to me, from 'Abd Allāh ibn Mas'ūd, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Amma ba'd, O assembly of Quraysh, you are fit for this affair as long as you do not disobey Allah. When you disobey Him, He will send over you one who will chastise you, just as this staff is chastised by a staff in his hand." Then he struck his staff, and it was white and hard.

He said in (al-Madārij):

As for preserving faith: faith, according to all the People of the Sunnah, increases with obedience and decreases with disobedience. Al-Shāfi'ī and others have reported this from the Companions, the Successors and those after them.

That disobediences weaken faith is a matter known by taste and experience. The servant, as the hadith states, "when he sins, a black spot is marked on his heart.

If he repents and seeks forgiveness, his heart is polished.

If he returns and sins, another spot is marked upon it, until it covers his heart.

That is the rān of which Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 14]."

Ugly deeds blacken the heart and extinguish its light, while faith is a light in the heart. Ugly deeds certainly remove it or diminish it.

Good deeds increase the light of the heart, and evil deeds extinguish the light of the heart.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has informed that the earning of hearts is a cause of the rān that covers them.

(Section)

Sound unveiling (al-mukāshafah al-ṣaḥīḥah): knowledges which the Lord, glory be to Him and exalted, produces in the heart of the servant, and by which He makes him aware of matters hidden from others. He may continue them, or withhold them from him through heedlessness of them, and conceal them from him by the ghayn that covers his heart, which is the subtlest of veils, or by the ghaym (cloud), which is thicker than it, or by the rān, which is the strongest of them.

The first occurs to the Prophets, peace be upon them, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, there comes over my heart, and I seek forgiveness from Allah more than seventy times."

The second occurs to the believers.

The third is for one upon whom wretchedness has prevailed. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 14].

Ibn 'Abbās and others said: It is sin after sin, covering the heart until it becomes like rān upon it.

The veils are ten. The first: the veil of ta'ṭīl (denial), negating the realities of the Names and Attributes, which is the thickest of them. For the possessor of this veil, it is not possible to know Allah, nor to reach Him at all, except as it is possible for a stone to ascend upward.

The second: the veil of shirk (association), which is that his heart devotes worship to other than Allah.

The third: the veil of verbal innovation (bid'ah qawliyyah), like the veil of the people of desires and corrupt doctrines, with their differences.

The fourth: the veil of practical innovation (bid'ah 'amaliyyah), like the veil of the innovating people of the path in their way and conduct.

The fifth: the veil of the people of hidden major sins, like the veil of the people of arrogance, self-admiration, showing off, envy, boasting, pride and the like.

The sixth: the veil of the people of manifest major sins. Their veil is thinner than the veil of their brethren from the people of hidden major sins, despite their abundant worship, asceticism and striving. Their major sins are closer to repentance than those of the others, for those have become stations for them which they do not shy away from displaying and presenting in the forms of worship and knowledge. So the people of manifest major sins are nearer to safety than they are.

And their hearts are better than their hearts.

The seventh: the veil of the people of minor sins.

The eighth: the veil of the people of excess and extravagance in permissible things.

The ninth: the veil of the people who are heedless of recalling what they were created for and what is required of them, and of what is due to Allah from them: constant remembrance, gratitude and servitude.

The tenth: the veil of the striving seekers, who exert themselves in the journey and are distracted from the goal.

These are ten veils between the heart and Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, which stand between it and this matter. These veils arise from four elements: the element of the self (nafs), the element of Satan, the element of this world (dunyā), and the element of desire (hawā). It is impossible to remove these veils while their roots and elements remain in the heart at all.

These four elements corrupt speech, action, intention and the path, according to their dominance or scarcity. They cut off the path of speech, action and intention from reaching the heart; and whatever reaches the heart, they cut off its path from reaching the Lord. Between speech and action on one side and the heart on the other is a distance in which the servant travels to his heart to see its wonders; and in this distance are the highwaymen mentioned. If he fights them, and the action reaches his heart, it circulates within it and seeks passage from there to Allah, for it does not settle short of reaching Him: ﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾ [al-Najm: 42]. When it reaches Allah, glory be to Him, He rewards it with an increase in his faith, certainty, knowledge and intellect, and adorns his outward and inward with it, guiding him by it to the best of morals and deeds, and turning away from him through it the evil of morals and deeds. Allah, glory be to Him, raises from that action for the heart an army with which it fights the highwaymen to reach Him. It fights the world by renunciation of it and by removing it from the heart, and it does not harm him if it is in his hand or house, nor does that prevent the strength of his certainty in the Hereafter. It fights Satan by refusing to respond to the call of desire, for Satan does not part from desire. It fights desire by submitting to the absolute command and standing with it, so that no desire remains for him in what he does or leaves. And it fights the self by the strength of sincerity.

All of this is when the action finds an outlet from the heart to the Lord, glory be to Him and exalted. But if it circulates within it and finds no outlet, and the self prevails over it, seizes it and makes it an army for itself, then it storms with it, rises and transgresses. You see him as the most ascetic, the most devout and the most diligent, yet he is the furthest from Allah, while the people of major sins are nearer to Allah in heart than he, and closer to sincerity and deliverance than he.

Look at the one who prostrates much, the worshipper, the ascetic, between whose eyes is the mark of prostration: how the excess of his action led him to object to the Prophet (ﷺ), and led his companions to despise the Muslims, until they drew their swords against them and made their blood lawful.

And look at the drunkard, the habitual drinker, who was often brought to the Prophet (ﷺ) and was flogged for drinking: how the strength of his faith, certainty, love for Allah and His Messenger, humility and submission to Allah remained in him, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade cursing him.

Thus it became evident from this that the excess of sins is safer in outcome than the excess of acts of obedience.

Imam Aḥmad related in the Kitāb al-Zuhd that Allah, glory be to Him, revealed to Moses (ﷺ): "O Moses, warn the truthful (ṣiddīqīn), for I do not place My justice upon anyone without punishing him, without wronging him. And give good tidings to the sinners, for no sin is too great for Me to forgive."

Let us return to explaining his words.

His saying: "A sound unveiling that indicates the sound verification (taḥqīq)." Everyone claims that the sound verification is with him.

And all claim the union with Layla,
but Layla does not acknowledge them in that.

When tears mingle on cheeks,
it becomes clear who weeps from who feigns weeping.

So sound verification is nothing but that which agrees with the reality of the matter itself. In knowledge, it is the unveiling that agrees with what the Messengers reported; in will, it is the unveiling that agrees with the religious will (murād dīnī) of the Lord from His servant. Our saying "religious" is a precaution against His cosmic will (murād kawnī), for everything in the cosmos is the consequence of this will.

So sound unveiling is that he knows the Truth with which Allah sent His Messengers and revealed His Books, by direct witnessing (mu'āyanah) in his heart, and he strips the will of his heart for it, so that it revolves with it in existence and non-existence. This is the sound verification, and whatever contradicts it is ugly delusion (ghurūr).

**Section: On using this verse to establish that the believers will see their Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, with their eyes, openly, as one sees the moon on the night of the full moon**

The argument from this verse is that God, glorified and exalted, made being veiled from seeing Him and from hearing His speech among the greatest punishments of the disbelievers. If the believers did not see Him and did not hear His speech, they too would be veiled from Him. Al-Shafi'i himself and other imams argued with this reasoning. Al-Tabarani and others, citing al-Muzani, reported: "I heard al-Shafi'i say, concerning the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿No indeed! Surely they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾, that there is in it evidence that the friends of God will see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Hakim said: Al-Asamm informed us, al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: "I was present with Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i when a note came to him from Sa'id (Egypt) asking what he said about the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿No indeed! Surely they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾. Al-Shafi'i said: 'Since these were veiled in wrath, there is in this evidence that His friends will see Him in good pleasure.' Al-Rabi' said: 'I said, O Abu 'Abd Allah, and do you say this?' He said: 'Yes, and by it I worship God. Had Muhammad ibn Idris not been certain that he would see God, he would not have worshipped the Mighty and Majestic.'"

Al-Tabarani also narrated it in *Sharh al-Sunnah* through the chain of al-Asamm.

Abu Zur'ah al-Razi said: I heard Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn say: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hakam was asked: "Will all creatures see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, believers and disbelievers?" Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah said: "None will see Him except the believers." Muhammad said: Al-Shafi'i was asked about the vision, and he said: God, the Exalted, says: ﴿No indeed! Surely they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾.

In this there is evidence that the believers are not veiled from God, the Mighty and Majestic.

**Section: On the threat against those who deny the vision**

The saying of God, the Exalted, ﴿No indeed! Surely they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾ has already been mentioned, along with the saying of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak: "God does not veil anyone from Himself except that He punishes him." Then he recited the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿Then surely they will burn in Hellfire. Then it will be said: "This is what you used to deny."﴾

He said: this is about the vision.

Muslim in his *Sahih* narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: They said: "O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Do you suffer any harm in seeing the sun at midday when there is no cloud?" They said: "No." He said: "Do you suffer any harm in seeing the moon on the night of the full moon when there is no cloud?" They said: "No." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will not suffer harm in seeing your Lord, except as you suffer harm in seeing one of them." He said: "Then He will meet the servant and say: 'O so-and-so, did I not honour you, make you a master, marry you, subject the horses and camels to you, and leave you to lead and take the quarter?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'Did you think that you would meet Me?' He will say: 'No.' He will say: 'Then I forget you as you forgot Me.' Then He will meet the second and say to him the same. Then He will meet the third and say to him the same, and he will say: 'O Lord, I believed in You, in Your Book, and in Your messengers, I prayed, fasted, and gave charity,' and he will praise himself with good as much as he can. He will say: 'Here then.' Then it will be said to him: 'Now We will send Our witness against you,' and he will think to himself: 'Who is the one who will testify against me?' His mouth will be sealed, and his thigh, his flesh, and his bones will be told: 'Speak.' So his thigh, his flesh, and his bones will speak of his deeds. This is so that he has no excuse before himself. That is the hypocrite, and that is the one with whom God is angry."

So combine His saying, "Surely you will see your Lord," with His saying to the one who thought he would not meet Him, "Then I forget you as you forgot Me."

The consensus of the scholars of the Arabic language (*ahl al-lughah*) is that meeting (*liqa'*) means seeing with the eyes. From this you come to know that the denier of the vision is more deserving of this threat.

Among the chapter headings of the People of the Sunnah (*Ahl al-Sunnah*) on this hadith is a chapter on the threat against those who deny the vision, as Shaykh al-Islam and others did. And success is from God.

**[Section: Some of the punishments for sins]**

Among them is the veiling of the heart from the Lord in this world, and the greater veil on the Day of Resurrection, as the Exalted said: ﴿No indeed! Rather, what they have earned has covered over their hearts. No indeed! Surely they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 14-15].

Sins prevented them from covering the distance between them and their hearts, so that they might reach them and see what makes them righteous and purified, and what corrupts and wretches them. And they were prevented from covering the distance between their hearts and their Lord, so that the hearts might reach Him and win nearness to Him and His honour, and be comforted by Him, and find peace in Him. Rather, the sins became a veil between them and their Lord and Creator.

He said in *Ighathat al-Lahfan*:

The Exalted said concerning the disbelievers: ﴿No indeed! Surely they will be veiled from their Lord that Day. Then surely they will burn in Hellfire﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15-16].

So He combined for them two kinds of punishment: the punishment of the Fire, and the punishment of being veiled from Him, glorified be He. Just as He combined for His friends two kinds of bliss: the bliss of enjoying what is in Paradise, and the bliss of enjoying the vision of Him.

He mentioned these four kinds in this surah, saying concerning the righteous: ﴿Surely the righteous will be in bliss, upon couches, gazing﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 22-23].

Whoever said that the meaning of the verse is "they look at their enemies being punished," or "they look at their palaces and gardens," or "some of them look at others," has distorted the meaning of the verse. All of this is a turning away from the intended meaning to something else. The meaning is only: they gaze at the face of their Lord, in contrast to the state of the disbelievers, who are veiled from their Lord.

﴿Then surely they will burn in Hellfire﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 16].

**(Section)**

The life of the lover with his beloved, without whom his heart, spirit, and life have no stability, and from whom he has no independence for the blink of an eye, and in whom there is no coolness for his eye, no tranquillity for his heart, and no rest for his spirit except through Him. He is more in need of Him than of his hearing, sight, and strength, and even more than of his life. For his life without Him is torment, pains, anxieties, and sorrows. So his life depends on nearness to Him, love for Him, and companionship with Him. The torment of being veiled from Him is greater than the other torment, just as the bliss of the heart and spirit through the removal of that veil is greater than the bliss of eating, drinking, and enjoying the dark-eyed maidens. Likewise, the punishment of the veil is greater than the punishment of the Blazing Fire. That is why God, glorified be He, combined for His friends the two blisses in His saying: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. The "best" is Paradise, and the "more" is the vision of His noble face in the Gardens of Eden.

And He combined for His enemies the two punishments in His saying: ﴿No indeed! Surely they will be veiled from their Lord that Day. Then surely they will burn in Hellfire﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15-16].

The point is that heedlessness is the slumber of the heart from seeking this life, and it is a veil over it. If this veil is not removed by remembrance, it thickens until it becomes a veil of idleness, play, and occupation with what does not benefit. If he hastens to remove it, and does not, it thickens until it becomes a veil of sins and minor transgressions that distance him from God. If he hastens to remove it, and does not, it thickens until it becomes a veil of major sins that bring about the Lord's hatred, wrath, and curse. If he hastens to remove it, and does not, it thickens until it becomes a veil of practical innovations, by which the doer torments himself and which benefit him nothing. If he hastens to remove it, and does not, it thickens until it becomes a veil of verbal and doctrinal innovations, which include lying against God and His Messenger, and denying the truth that the Messenger brought. If he hastens to remove it, and does not, it thickens until it becomes a veil of doubt and denial, which undermines the five foundations of faith, which are: belief in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and meeting Him. Because of the severity, density, darkness, and blackness of this veil, he does not see the realities of faith, and Satan takes hold of him, promising him and raising his hopes.

The commanding self (*al-nafs al-ammarah bi-l-su'*) desires and craves, and the sovereignty of nature has overcome the sovereignty of faith, imprisoned it, and jailed it, if not destroyed it. It has taken over the management of the kingdom and the employment of the armies of desires, and has assigned to them the habits in which action has been carried on. It has closed the gate of wakefulness and set over it the gatekeeper of heedlessness, and said: "Beware lest we be attacked from your side." It has appointed a chamberlain from among the desires, and said: "Beware lest you allow anyone to enter upon me except with you. The affair of this kingdom has come to you and to the gatekeeper. So O gatekeeper of heedlessness, and O chamberlain of desire, let each of you hold his frontier. If you abandon it, the affairs of our kingdom will be corrupted, and the state will return to others, and the sovereignty of faith will inflict upon us the worst disgrace and humiliation, and we will never again rejoice in this city."

There is no god but God! When these armies gather upon the heart, along with the weakness of faith, the scarcity of helpers, turning away from the remembrance of the Merciful, joining the ranks of the sons of this age, and long hope which corrupts the human being, so that he prefers the immediate and present over the absent promised thing after these worlds are folded up. So God is the one sought for help, and upon Him is reliance.

Ibn al-Qayyim, commentary on Surah 83 (al-Mutaffifin), verses 18–20:

He, the Exalted, informed that their book is a "marqum" (inscribed) book, as an affirmation, because it is written in a true, literal writing.

And the Exalted singled out the book of the righteous (al-abrar): that it is written and sealed for them in the presence of those brought near (al-muqarrabun) among the angels and the prophets, the chiefs of the believers.

He did not mention the testimony of these to the book of the wicked (al-fujjar), in order to honor the book of the righteous and what was recorded for them in it, and to publicize it and make manifest their station among the elite of His creation, just as kings write decrees (tawaqi') which are honored among the princes and the elite of the kingdom, to give prominence to the name of the one for whom they are written and to publicize his mention.

And this is a kind of the blessing (salah) of Allah, the Exalted, and His angels upon His servant.

And he said in (Tariq al-Hijratayn):

And He informed that the muqarrabun witness their book, meaning it is written in their presence and before their eyes, and they are not absent from it, out of care for it and to manifest the honor of its owner and his station with his Lord.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 83, verse 26:

Alqama reported from Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿Its seal is musk﴾. He said: "It is mixed, and it is not sealed afterward."

I (Ibn al-Qayyim) say: He means, and God knows best, that its last part is musk mixed into it, so it belongs to the aftertaste (al-khatima) and not to the sealing (al-khatm).

Zayd ibn Mu'awiya said: I asked Alqama about the words of the Exalted: ﴿Its seal is musk﴾, and I read it as (khatamuhu misk) [its seal, musk]. He said to me: "It is not khatamuhu, but recite it as ﴿khitamuhu misk﴾."

Alqama said: "Khitamuhu means its mixture. Do you not see that a woman among your women says of perfume, that its mixture is of musk, such and such."

Sa'id ibn Mansur mentioned: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murra, from Masruq: "Al-raheeq is wine, al-makhtum: they find its end has the taste of musk."

And with this same chain, from Masruq, from Abdullah, regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿And its mixture is of Tasnim﴾, he said: "It is mixed for the people of the right hand, and the near ones drink it pure." Likewise Ibn Abbas said: "The near ones drink from it pure, and it is mixed for those below them."

Mujahid said: "Khitamuhu misk" means "clay." This interpretation requires its own explanation, and the wording of the verse is clearer than it. It seems, and God knows best, that he means the sediment that remains at the bottom of the vessel.

Al-Hakim mentioned from the hadith of Adam: Shaybaan narrated to us, from Jabir, from Ibn Sabit, from Abu al-Darda regarding His words ﴿Its seal is musk﴾:

He said: "It is a white drink like silver, with which they seal their last drink. If a man of the people of this world were to put his hand into it and then take it out, no living soul would remain without finding the scent of its fragrance."

(Section)

Al-munafasa is the complete desire for a thing and preventing others from it, if sharing is not praised in it; and racing toward it if sharing is praised in it. The Exalted said: ﴿And for that let the competitors compete﴾.

Between munafasa and ghibta there is both union and difference, and between them and envy (hasad) there is also both union and difference.

So munafasa includes racing, striving and eagerness.

Envy indicates the lowliness and incapacity of the envier; otherwise, compete with the one you envy.

That is more beneficial for you than his envy, as it is said:

"When the qualities of a man please you, become like him and you will become what pleases you.
For there is no gate to generosity and noble qualities that a doorkeeper bars you from when you come to it."

Ghibta includes a kind of wonder and joy for the one envied, and approval of his state.

[Section: The difference between munafasa and envy]

The difference between munafasa and envy: munafasa is hastening toward a perfection that you witness in another, so you compete with him for it until you catch up with him or surpass him. It comes from the nobility of the soul, the height of aspiration and the greatness of rank. The Exalted said: ﴿And for that let the competitors compete﴾.

Its root is from a precious thing to which souls cling with desire and longing, so each of the two souls competes for it with the other, and at times it rejoices when it shares it with the other. Likewise, the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to compete in good, and some of them rejoiced in others because they shared in it; rather, some urged others toward it while competing for it. It is a kind of racing. The Exalted said: ﴿So race toward the good deeds﴾.

And the Exalted said: ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven﴾. Umar ibn al-Khattab used to race Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with them both), and he never won the race ahead of him. When he realized that Abu Bakr had taken the lead in leadership, he said: "By God, I will never race you to anything again." And he said: "By God, I never preceded him to any good except that I found he had already preceded me to it."

Two competitors are like two servants before their master, who vie and compete in pleasing him and race toward what he loves. Their master is pleased with that from them and urges them toward it, and each of them loves the other and encourages him to please their master.

Envy is the trait of a base, lowly and fallen soul, in which there is no eagerness for good. Due to its incapacity and lowliness, it envies whoever gains good and praiseworthy qualities and succeeds in them beyond it, and it wishes that its own failure to gain them would make it equal to him in nothingness, as the Exalted said: ﴿They wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved, so that you would be equal﴾.

And the Exalted said: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could return you to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them﴾.

So the envier is an enemy of the blessing, wishing for its removal from the one envied, as it has been removed from him. The competitor is one who hastens toward the blessing, wishing its completion for himself and for the one he competes with. He should aspire to surpass him, love to catch up with him or to exceed him in virtue. The envier loves the decline of others until he is equal to him in deficiency. Most virtuous and good souls benefit from munafasa. Whoever keeps before his eyes a person of virtue and precedence and competes with him benefits greatly from him, for he imitates him and seeks to catch up with him and advance beyond him. This you do not blame. The name "envy" is sometimes applied to praiseworthy competition, as in the authentic report from the Prophet (ﷺ):

"There is no envy except in two: a man whom God has given the Qur'an, so he stands with it through the hours of the night and the ends of the day; and a man whom God has given wealth, so he spends it in truth."

So this is envy of competition and ghibta, which indicates the lofty aspiration of its possessor, the greatness of his soul, and his seeking to resemble the people of virtue.

Tasnim: the highest of the drinks of Paradise. So He, glory be to Him, informed that the mixture of the drink of the righteous (al-abrar) is from Tasnim, and that those brought near (al-muqarrabun) drink from it unmixed. For this reason He said: ﴿a spring from which those brought near will drink﴾, as He, exalted is He, said in Surat al-Insan likewise.

Ibn 'Abbas and others said: "Those brought near drink from it pure (sarfan), and it is mixed for the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin) as a mixture (mazjan)."

This is because the recompense corresponds to the deed (wifaq al-'amal). Just as the deeds of those brought near were all purified for Allah, their drink was purified; and just as the righteous mixed their acts of obedience with permissible things, their drink was mixed for them. So whoever is sincere, his drink is made pure, and whoever mixes, his drink is mixed.

Poetry:

O you who are heedless in the flood of ignorance and desire,
Lying prostrate on the beds of destruction, tossing about,

Reflect, may Allah guide you, and wake up, for this is the drink of the people in truth, it is blended (yurakkab).

Its blending in this abode, if you are diligent, has no seeking after death.

Oh, how strange is one who turns away from his life and from his lofty portion, and amuses himself and plays!

And if the deprived one knew what merchandise he had wasted, his heart would be ablaze.

If he does not know, that is a calamity; and if he knows, the calamity is harder still.

Indeed, he will know when the veil is lifted, and he will be stripped bare, wailing and lamenting.

He marvels at one who sold something for less than its worth without knowledge, yet your own case is more marvelous.

For you have sold life and its goodness for the pleasure of a dream that will soon pass away.

Why did you not reverse the matter, if you were resolute? But you wasted resolve, and the decree prevails.

You turn away and keep distant from your Beloved always; where, woe to you, will you go from the Beloved?

You will know on the Day of Gathering what trade you wasted, when those scales are set up.

(Fa'idah)

He said in Surat al-Mutaffifin about the drink of the righteous: ﴿And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which those brought near will drink﴾

And He said: ﴿from which those brought near will drink﴾ and did not say "from it" (minha), indicating that their drinking is by the spring itself, purely, not by it and something else.

So He included in (yashrabu) the meaning of (yarwa) (to quench/be satisfied), and so it takes the preposition (bi). This is a subtler derivation and better in meaning than making the bi mean (min), but rather including in the verb (yashrabu) the meaning of another verb, so that it takes its transitivity. This is the method of the skilled grammarians, and it is the method of Sibawayh and the leading figures of his school.

And about the righteous He said: ﴿They drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor﴾ [al-Insan: 5], because the drinking of those brought near is more perfect, so the preposition bi indicating drinking to quench is used for them with the spring pure. The Qur'an's indication is subtler and more eloquent than that humans can encompass.

Tasnim: the highest of the drinks of Paradise. So He, glory be to Him, informed that the mixture of the drink of the righteous (al-abrar) is from Tasnim, and that those brought near (al-muqarrabun) drink from it unmixed. For this reason He said: ﴿a spring from which those brought near will drink﴾, as He, exalted is He, said in Surat al-Insan likewise.

Ibn 'Abbas and others said: "Those brought near drink from it pure (sarfan), and it is mixed for the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin) as a mixture (mazjan)."

This is because the recompense corresponds to the deed (wifaq al-'amal). Just as the deeds of those brought near were all purified for Allah, their drink was purified; and just as the righteous mixed their acts of obedience with permissible things, their drink was mixed for them. So whoever is sincere, his drink is made pure, and whoever mixes, his drink is mixed.

Poetry:

O you who are heedless in the flood of ignorance and desire,
Lying prostrate on the beds of destruction, tossing about,

Reflect, may Allah guide you, and wake up, for this is the drink of the people in truth, it is blended (yurakkab).

Its blending in this abode, if you are diligent, has no seeking after death.

Oh, how strange is one who turns away from his life and from his lofty portion, and amuses himself and plays!

And if the deprived one knew what merchandise he had wasted, his heart would be ablaze.

If he does not know, that is a calamity; and if he knows, the calamity is harder still.

Indeed, he will know when the veil is lifted, and he will be stripped bare, wailing and lamenting.

He marvels at one who sold something for less than its worth without knowledge, yet your own case is more marvelous.

For you have sold life and its goodness for the pleasure of a dream that will soon pass away.

Why did you not reverse the matter, if you were resolute? But you wasted resolve, and the decree prevails.

You turn away and keep distant from your Beloved always; where, woe to you, will you go from the Beloved?

You will know on the Day of Gathering what trade you wasted, when those scales are set up.

(Fa'idah)

He said in Surat al-Mutaffifin about the drink of the righteous: ﴿And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which those brought near will drink﴾

And He said: ﴿from which those brought near will drink﴾ and did not say "from it" (minha), indicating that their drinking is by the spring itself, purely, not by it and something else.

So He included in (yashrabu) the meaning of (yarwa) (to quench/be satisfied), and so it takes the preposition (bi). This is a subtler derivation and better in meaning than making the bi mean (min), but rather including in the verb (yashrabu) the meaning of another verb, so that it takes its transitivity. This is the method of the skilled grammarians, and it is the method of Sibawayh and the leading figures of his school.

And about the righteous He said: ﴿They drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor﴾ [al-Insan: 5], because the drinking of those brought near is more perfect, so the preposition bi indicating drinking to quench is used for them with the spring pure. The Qur'an's indication is subtler and more eloquent than that humans can encompass.

Consider how He, glorified is He, answered what the disbelievers said about the believers in this world, when they mocked them, with its opposite on the Day of Resurrection. For the disbelievers, whenever the believers passed by them, would wink at one another and laugh at them: ﴿And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are the misguided"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 32].

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So today, those who believed will be laughing at the disbelievers﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 34], as a counterpart to their winking and laughing at them.

Then He said: "Looking" without restriction, and He did not limit it to one object of sight over another. The highest, most exalted and greatest thing they look at is Allah, glorified is He. Looking at Him is the most sublime and excellent kind of looking, and it is the highest rank of guidance. Thus He answered their saying ﴿Indeed, these are misguided﴾ with this.

So the looking at the Lord, glorified is He, is intended in both of these verses without doubt, either specifically or in general and unrestricted form.

Whoever reflects on the context will find that the two verses cannot bear any meaning other than this intention, whether specifically or generally.
